prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe (refs #2431)
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError-family exceptions don't survive pickle/unpickle round-trips (tracked as #2431). Root cause: MCPError.__init__ sets Exception.args to (code, message, data), and default Exception.__reduce__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args). That works for MCPError itself, but UrlElicitationRequiredError overrides __init__ with signature (elicitations, message=None) — so unpickling calls the subclass with 3 positional args it doesn't accept, raising TypeError. Both PRs patch src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py to fix exactly this. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError-family exceptions don't survive pickle/unpickle round-trips (tracked as #2431). That works for MCPError itself, but UrlElicitationRequiredError overrides __init__ with signature (elicitations, message=None) — so unpickling calls the subclass with 3 positional args it doesn't accept, raising TypeError. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs fix the same reported bug (#2431: UrlElicitationRequiredError raises TypeError on unpickle), but they differ in scope and risk. #2555 adds __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from the typed self._elicitations + message it already stores — a minimal, class-local change that doesn't alter pickle behavior for MCPError or any other subclass that already round-trips correctly via the default Exception.__reduce_ex__. It also ships a matching update to tests/shared/test_exceptions.py exercising the round trip. #2478 instead replaces reconstruction for the whole MCPError hierarchy with a module-level _restore_mcp_error dispatcher (from_error_data/from_error), which is a larger blast-radius change than the bug requires since only the one subclass was ever broken, and it bundles in an unrelated change (dropping '# pragma: no cover' on the data property) that isn't part of the pickle fix itself. Recommend closing #2478 in favor of #2555's narrower, better-scoped fix, porting over any test cases from #2478 that #2555 doesn't already cover.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing/colliding on the same in-flight JSON-RPC request id can cross-wire in `_request_streams`, causing one request to receive another's response or hang. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids where int 1 and string "1" both become "1" — this reintroduces the exact cross-wiring bug it's trying to fix whenever a client mixes numeric and string ids, and a string id equal to "_GET_stream" would collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 replaces the naive str() key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can't collide with GET_STREAM_KEY, so it covers both the case #3063 handles and the two edge cases #3063's approach leaves open.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs fix the same reported bug (#2431: UrlElicitationRequiredError raises TypeError on unpickle), but they differ in scope and risk. #2555 adds __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from the typed self._elicitations + message it already stores — a minimal, class-local change that doesn't alter pickle behavior for MCPError or any other subclass that already round-trips correctly via the default Exception.__reduce_ex__. It also ships a matching update to tests/shared/test_exceptions.py exercising the round trip. #2478 instead replaces reconstruction for the whole MCPError hierarchy with a module-level _restore_mcp_error dispatcher (from_error_data/from_error), which is a larger blast-radius change than the bug requires since only the one subclass was ever broken, and it bundles in an unrelated change (dropping '# pragma: no cover' on the data property) that isn't part of the pickle fix itself. Recommend closing #2478 in favor of #2555's narrower, better-scoped fix, porting over any test cases from #2478 that #2555 doesn't already cover.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids where int 1 and string "1" both become "1" — this reintroduces the exact cross-wiring bug it's trying to fix whenever a client mixes numeric and string ids, and a string id equal to "_GET_stream" would collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 replaces the naive str() key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can't collide with GET_STREAM_KEY, so it covers both the case #3063 handles and the two edge cases #3063's approach leaves open.

That still requires the doomed request and 401 to occur on every restart before recovering, whereas #1784 prevents the 401 from happening at all for this specific, named cause.

clusters.pick_reason: 2253 contains both halves of the fix: it adds the loop in terminate() that closes every writer in self._sse_stream_writers, and it changes streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan shutdown path to call terminate() on all active sessions before the task group is cancelled — the actual shutdown-ordering change. 3218's visible diff only adds registration of the GET/standalone-stream's writer into self._sse_stream_writers (a gap that matters only if a terminate()-side closing loop already exists); it doesn't show any corresponding change to the manager shutdown orchestration itself, so on its own it doesn't fully deliver the 'terminate sessions on manager shutdown' behavior its title claims.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs fix the same reported bug (#2431: UrlElicitationRequiredError raises TypeError on unpickle), but they differ in scope and risk. #2555 adds __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from the typed self._elicitations + message it already stores — a minimal, class-local change that doesn't alter pickle behavior for MCPError or any other subclass that already round-trips correctly via the default Exception.__reduce_ex__. It also ships a matching update to tests/shared/test_exceptions.py exercising the round trip. #2478 instead replaces reconstruction for the whole MCPError hierarchy with a module-level _restore_mcp_error dispatcher (from_error_data/from_error), which is a larger blast-radius change than the bug requires since only the one subclass was ever broken, and it bundles in an unrelated change (dropping '# pragma: no cover' on the data property) that isn't part of the pickle fix itself. Recommend closing #2478 in favor of #2555's narrower, better-scoped fix, porting over any test cases from #2478 that #2555 doesn't already cover.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: MCPError-family exceptions don't survive pickle/unpickle round-trips (tracked as #2431). Root cause: MCPError.__init__ sets Exception.args to (code, message, data), and default Exception.__reduce__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args). That works for MCPError itself, but UrlElicitationRequiredError overrides __init__ with signature (elicitations, message=None) — so unpickling calls the subclass with 3 positional args it doesn't accept, raising TypeError. Both PRs patch src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py to fix exactly this.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids where int 1 and string "1" both become "1" — this reintroduces the exact cross-wiring bug it's trying to fix whenever a client mixes numeric and string ids, and a string id equal to "_GET_stream" would collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 replaces the naive str() key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can't collide with GET_STREAM_KEY, so it covers both the case #3063 handles and the two edge cases #3063's approach leaves open.
